message.content:
The as-reported input cell is hexagonal in metric character: the two basal edges are recorded as [[param:cell.a]] and [[param:cell.b]], the unique axis as [[param:cell.c]], the basal-to-unique angles as [[param:cell.alpha]] and [[param:cell.beta]], and the basal angle as [[param:cell.gamma]]. Thus a and b have the same supplied length while gamma is marginally above the ideal hexagonal value; this is treated as an as-input deviation rather than an idealized correction, and no separate precision-correction terms are supplied. The input contents comprise [[param:input.atom_count]] atoms, chemically distributed as [[param:composition.Hg]], [[param:composition.Sn]], and [[param:composition.Sr]].

The symmetry is that of space group [[param:space_group.number]], with Hall symbol [[param:space_group.hall]], a primitive hexagonal polar setting in which the independent atoms are expanded by the public symmetry operations. The standard coordinate frame is coincident with the input frame: the basis transform is the identity [[param:frame.matrix]] and the origin displacement is zero [[param:frame.origin_shift]], so fractional coordinates in the standard setting can be read directly against the supplied cell, subject to the stated input fractional rounding of [[param:round_digits]] decimal places.

Three independent Wyckoff orbits account for the six atoms. Strontium occupies orbit [[param:orbit.o000.id]], assigned to element [[param:orbit.o000.element]] on Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o000.wyckoff]], with its single free coordinate given by [[param:orbit.o000.parameters]]; in the public expansion this is a multiplicity-two orbit lying on the polar axis at fractional positions of the form 0, 0, z, with only z free. Tin occupies orbit [[param:orbit.o001.id]], assigned to element [[param:orbit.o001.element]] on Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o001.wyckoff]], with free coordinate [[param:orbit.o001.parameters]]; it is likewise multiplicity two but uses the 1/3, 2/3, z coordinate relation, again free only along z. Mercury occupies orbit [[param:orbit.o002.id]], assigned to element [[param:orbit.o002.element]] on Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o002.wyckoff]], with free coordinate [[param:orbit.o002.parameters]]; it shares the same 1/3, 2/3, z public coordinate relation as the tin orbit while remaining crystallographically independent because its z parameter differs.
